title: Every lent scenario of the smoke tier failed at create on Linux, because the lender had no binary to run
foundBy: session agent, maintainer of this repository, running `make ci` before a push

evidence.verified: Before the change, `make ci` on a Linux host reached `test-smoke` and failed. Five scenarios were reported as `create-failed`, and each one had `exec: "cs-sandbox": executable file not found in $PATH` from the lender container. After the change, `make test-smoke` on the same host passed all six scenarios of `TestSmokeReplay` with exit 0, and left no sandbox behind.

details:
A lent scenario puts a credential lender on the campaign's network, and that container runs `cs-sandbox lender`. The slim image the test tiers boot carries no `cs-sandbox`. `cs-sandbox` copies one in only when `CS_SANDBOX_LENDER_BIN` names it, which is the change SBX-041 describes in the sandbox ledger.

The helper `ensureLiveLenderBinary` in `internal/cli/livecampaign_test.go` sets that variable, and it returned early on Linux. Its comment gave the reason: `cs-sandbox` mounted its own executable into the lender on Linux. That stopped being true when the pin moved onto the sandbox revision that holds SBX-041. From then on the lender container started and died at once on a Linux host, and the campaign reported only that create had failed.

The unit tier fakes `cs-sandbox`, so it could not see this. The smoke tier skips itself where a host cannot carry it, so a CI runner with no KVM could not see it either. It took a Linux host with KVM and a full `make ci`.

The helper now sets the variable on every host, and its comment says why.
